newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: High rates seen crimping South African shares.
newsitem.headline: High rates seen crimping South African shares.

text.p: High real interest rates and low growth will hold back the South Afrcan share market despite a valuation that compares favourably with other emerging markets, a global economic strategist said on Tuesday.

David Hale, global economic strategist with Zurch Kemper Investments of Chicago, told a Societe Generale Frankel Pollak investment conference that the consensus forecast for South African real GDP growth of 2.5-3.5 percent over the next few years was "not exciting".
It compared to 4.0-5.0 percent in much of Latin America and the Indian sub-continent, 6.0-9.0 percent in east Asia, and 5.0-6.0 percent in post-communist eastern Europe.
South Africa also has inflation of 8.0-10.0 percent and short-term interest rates of 17.00 percent, making for very high real rates.

High real rates in themselves were not necessarily a barrier to a strong stock market, provided growth was high, Hale said. But South African profits were projected to expand by 15-20 percent this year and next after just 12 percent in 1996 and 37 percent in 1995.

"As the prospective p/e multiple of the South African market is only about 12 today compared to 19 in Indonesia, 10 in Brazil, 14 in Argentina, 20 in Malaysia, 11 in Thailand and 10-12 in post-communist eastern Europe, it is not difficult to argue that equity investors should be able to find interesting opportunities in some sectors of the South African market," he said.
"But real interest rates will constrain the performance of the total market until there is a more compelling growth story to tell about South Africa beyond 1997, or interest rates decline."
